one_line: OpenAI raises funds, launches API; governments tighten AI rules; medical AI improves; compute capacity grows worldwide.

themes.title: OpenAI seeks funding, launches API
themes.text: OpenAI is negotiating a private funding round of up to $30 billion that would value the company at $1.25 trillion, and it has made its Decisions API with voice and visual inputs generally available.

stories.headline: OpenAI seeks up to $30 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of IPO
OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens

themes.title: Governments tighten AI regulations
themes.text: Swedish government ministries have prohibited staff from using ChatGPT and Claude, requiring Microsoft Copilot; India will issue a consultation paper on AI legislation; major U.S. banks are restricting third‑party AI agents from accessing customer accounts.

stories.headline: Swedish government offices ban ChatGPT and Claude, require Microsoft Copilot
India to issue AI law consultation paper in coming weeks, says minister
Major US banks block third‑party AI agents from customer accounts

themes.title: Medical AI diagnostic accuracy rises
themes.text: Microsoft’s Diagnostic Orchestrator correctly diagnosed complex medical cases 83% of the time in simulations, outperforming generalist physicians.

stories.headline: Microsoft AI diagnostic system hits 83% accuracy, over twice doctors in complex cases
Microsoft diagnostic orchestrator reaches 83% accuracy in complex case simulation

themes.title: AI compute capacity expands globally
themes.text: SpaceX plans to manage at least 13 GW of AI compute power by the end of 2027, and Kazakhstan is building a data center with 45,000 NVIDIA Grace GPUs targeting up to 500 MW capacity.

stories.headline: SpaceX aims for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027
Kazakhstan expands AI compute with 45,000 Grace GPUs and new data centers
